title: Dental Care

dialogue.title: Ahmed's Dental Checkup
dialogue.context: Ahmed schedules and attends his first dental appointment in the U.S.

lines.speaker: Ahmed
lines.text: Hello, I'd like to schedule a dental cleaning. It's been over a year since my last visit.

lines.speaker: Receptionist
lines.text: We can get you in next Tuesday at 2 PM. Is that okay? Please bring your insurance card.

lines.speaker: Ahmed
lines.text: Perfect, thank you. [At the appointment] Hi, I'm here for my 2 o'clock appointment.

lines.speaker: Hygienist
lines.text: Ahmed? Come on back. When was your last cleaning?

lines.speaker: Ahmed
lines.text: About 18 months ago, in my home country. I just moved to the U.S.

lines.speaker: Hygienist
lines.text: Welcome! Let me clean your teeth first, then Dr. Martinez will check for any problems. Do you floss regularly?

lines.speaker: Ahmed
lines.text: Honestly, not as much as I should. Maybe once or twice a week.

lines.speaker: Hygienist
lines.text: You should try to floss every day. It prevents gum disease and cavities between teeth. I'll show you the proper technique.

lines.speaker: Dr. Martinez
lines.text: Hi Ahmed, let me take a look. Your teeth look mostly good, but you have one small cavity on your back molar. We should fill it before it gets worse.

lines.speaker: Dr. Martinez
lines.text: Most dental insurance covers 80% of fillings. The receptionist can give you an exact cost estimate. The cavity is small, so the filling should be quick and painless.

lines.speaker: Ahmed
lines.text: Okay, let's schedule it. How can I prevent more cavities?

lines.speaker: Dr. Martinez
lines.text: Brush twice a day, floss daily, limit sugary foods and drinks, and come for cleanings every six months. You're doing great by coming in now!

pattern_drills.pattern: How often should I [dental care action]?
examples: How often should I brush my teeth?
How often should I get a cleaning?
How often should I replace my toothbrush?
How often should I see the dentist?

listening_exercises.transcript: Proper dental care includes brushing twice daily for two minutes each time, flossing once a day, and visiting the dentist every six months for cleanings. Use a soft-bristle toothbrush and fluoride toothpaste. Replace your toothbrush every 3-4 months. Flossing removes plaque and food between teeth where brushes can't reach.
listening_exercises.question: How often should you visit the dentist?

listening_exercises.transcript: A cavity is a hole in your tooth caused by decay. Bacteria in your mouth produce acid that damages tooth enamel. Early cavities can be reversed with fluoride treatments, but larger cavities need fillings. Warning signs include tooth sensitivity to hot, cold, or sweet foods, visible holes or pits, and toothache.
listening_exercises.question: What causes cavities?

listening_exercises.transcript: Dental insurance typically covers preventive care like cleanings and exams at 100%. Basic procedures like fillings are usually covered at 70-80%. Major procedures like crowns and root canals might be covered at 50%. Most plans have an annual maximum of $1000-2000. Always check with your insurance before expensive procedures.
listening_exercises.question: What do dental plans usually cover at 100%?

speaking_tasks.prompt: Call to schedule a dental cleaning. Say: you need a cleaning, you haven't been in a year, ask about available times. Record for 20 seconds.
speaking_tasks.example: Hello, I'd like to schedule a dental cleaning please. It's been about a year since my last visit. Do you have any availability this week or next week? I'm flexible with the time - mornings or afternoons work for me. Also, do I need to bring anything specific? Thank you!

speaking_tasks.prompt: Explain good dental care habits to a friend. Give at least 3 tips. Record for 25 seconds.
speaking_tasks.example: Let me tell you about good dental care. First, brush your teeth twice a day for at least two minutes each time. Use fluoride toothpaste. Second, floss every single day to clean between your teeth where the brush can't reach. Third, limit sugary foods and drinks because sugar causes cavities. Fourth, see your dentist every six months for a professional cleaning. These habits will keep your teeth healthy!

writing_tasks.prompt: Describe your dental care routine. How often do you brush? Do you floss? When was your last dentist visit? (50-60 words)
writing_tasks.example: I brush my teeth twice a day - once in the morning after breakfast and once before bed. I use fluoride toothpaste and a soft toothbrush. I try to floss every day, but honestly I sometimes forget. My last dentist visit was about eight months ago for a routine cleaning. The hygienist said my teeth look good but I need to floss more consistently. I'm scheduled for my next cleaning in four months.

writing_tasks.prompt: You have a toothache. Write what you would say when calling the dentist for an emergency appointment. (40-50 words)
writing_tasks.example: Hello, I'm calling because I have a severe toothache. The pain started yesterday and it's getting worse. My back tooth hurts when I eat or drink anything. Do you have any emergency appointments available today or tomorrow? I'm a current patient - my name is Ahmed Hassan. The pain is really bad and I need to see someone soon.

grammar_focus.title: 'Need + noun/infinitive' for Dental Care
grammar_focus.explanation: Use 'need + noun' or 'need + to + verb' to talk about dental care requirements.
examples: You need to floss daily. (need + to + verb)
They need to see a dentist. (need + to + verb)

grammar_focus.title: 'Prevent/Avoid + gerund' for Prevention
grammar_focus.explanation: Use 'prevent' or 'avoid' with gerund (-ing form) to talk about preventing dental problems.
examples: Avoid eating too much sugar. (avoid + gerund)
Brushing prevents developing gum disease. (prevent + gerund)

grammar_focus.title: Passive Voice for Procedures
grammar_focus.explanation: Dental procedures are often described using passive voice (be + past participle).
examples: Your teeth will be cleaned. (passive - focus on teeth, not person cleaning)
The cavity was filled. (passive - describing what happened)
X-rays are taken annually. (passive - regular procedure)
The tooth needs to be extracted. (passive - necessary action)

cultural_notes: Dental care is expensive in the U.S. Many people have dental insurance through their jobs.
Children often get fluoride treatments and sealants to prevent cavities.
Many Americans whiten their teeth - white teeth are considered attractive in U.S. culture.
Dentists recommend electric toothbrushes over manual ones.
Dental emergencies can be treated at emergency dental clinics, though they're expensive.
Some people go to Mexico or other countries for cheaper dental work (called 'dental tourism').
